clue.text: Celebration called for — the fifty's up!

definitions.text: Celebration called for — the fifty's up!

parts.words: Celebration called for — the fifty's up!
parts.note: the whole clue describes the festivity held when fifty years of a reign or marriage have been completed

explanation.surface: Someone's fiftieth year has arrived and a party is demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: A jubilee is traditionally a fiftieth anniversary, so 'the fifty's up' points to the half-century mark that calls for the celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A jubilee is an anniversary festival, classically marking fifty years.

clue.text: Old City one was angrily told to visit

definitions.meaning: an ancient city of the Jordan valley whose walls fell in the Bible

definitions.text: one was angrily told to visit
definitions.meaning: the old dismissive phrase 'go to' this place told someone to clear off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to Jericho!' was an old way of telling someone angrily to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city whose walls fell to Joshua's trumpets was also the place in the old curse 'go to' it.

clue.text: How to cast girls in Macbeth -making entrances

definitions.text: How to cast girls in Macbeth
definitions.meaning: split as '...', the role three actresses take in Shakespeare's play
to entrance is to put under a spell or enchant

explanation.walkthrough: 'making' links the two parts. Read the answer as BE WITCHES for the casting note; 'entrances' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not doorways.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to cast a spell, and the three hags in Shakespeare's Scottish play are the weird sisters.

clue.text: Tree in a musical play-that was ahead of time

definitions.meaning: a flowering shrub or small tree with fragrant mauve or white blossom

definitions.text: in a musical play-that was ahead of time
definitions.meaning: the operetta '... Time', where this word comes just before 'Time'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lilac Time' was a popular operetta about Schubert; the word sits ahead of 'Time' in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The mauve-flowered shrub is a small tree, and it is the word placed before 'Time' in the operetta title.

clue.text: Macaroni? Delicious!

definitions.meaning: an 18th-century fop who affected Continental fashions
extremely fine or delightful to taste

explanation.walkthrough: 'Macaroni' looks like pasta but is the old word for a dandy; another old word for such a fop is the answer as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy was once called an exquisite, and the adjective also means superbly fine or delightful.

clue.text: Isis's rattle is in play, after a fashion

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us to place the clue's 'is' within the word for playing loosely

parts.note: to strum is to play an instrument casually or crudely, playing after a fashion

explanation.surface: A rattle sacred to the goddess Isis is being played, though not very well.
explanation.walkthrough: The sistrum was the metal rattle shaken in the worship of the Egyptian goddess Isis; 'is' is fodder here, not a link, with 'in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sistrum is an ancient Egyptian percussion instrument shaken in rites of the goddess.

clue.text: In assault, be violent

definitions.meaning: a sudden attack on a fortified place
to rage furiously, like wind and rain

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops take a fortress by sudden attack, and a tempest rages violently.

clue.text: Nightly Illumination of neons above play title?

definitions.meaning: the faint glow given by stars at night
the lead actor's name in lights over a theatre show's title

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the two senses; the second reads the answer as two words, the star's name lit up in neon outside the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the stars glows at night, and a headliner's name is lit in neon over a show title.

clue.text: The birds of Waterloo

parts.note: marsh birds that share a name with the metal tracks of a London railway terminus

explanation.surface: A question about which birds live at a famous battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the battle, but it is the London railway station, and its tracks share a name with a family of marsh birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Small wading birds of the marsh share a name with the steel tracks of a station.

clue.text: Darlings, they're a servile lot!

definitions.meaning: favourites, as a king's pet courtiers
fawning underlings who do a master's bidding

explanation.definitionFit: A favourite of a prince was a darling, and the word now means slavish followers.

clue.text: If in distress, lower a stimulant

indicators.note: being in distress suggests the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: If someone is in trouble, let down something to revive them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' rearranges LOWER. A rowel is the spiked wheel of a spur, something that urges a horse on, hence a stimulant.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiked wheel on a rider's spur goads a horse forward, so it acts as a goad or incentive.

clue.text: Price asked for the words of another

definitions.meaning: a seller's stated charge for a job or goods
a passage repeated from someone else's speech or writing

explanation.walkthrough: The held clue has a stray '14' that the printed page does not show; the clue is a plain double definition, joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's estimate is a quote, and a cited passage from an author is also a quote.

clue.text: Quiz about a poor chemist

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: a poor version of a word is a badly formed one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A test is set concerning a pharmacist who is not very good.
explanation.walkthrough: A catechism is a set of questions and answers used in religious instruction, so 'Quiz' is fair; 'poor' scrambles the chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is instruction given through a fixed series of questions and replies, a kind of examination.

clue.text: How to catch a donkey — look out!

indicators.note: here 'out' says the word for look sits on the outside of the animal

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A warning shout as someone tries to capture a stray donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look out' reads as a warning shout, but 'out' is the container signal. A lasso is a rope loop used to catch animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat with a running noose is the cowboy's means of capturing livestock.

clue.text: Gold round the middle isn't the same

indicators.note: the heraldic gold word goes round the outside of the next word
the clue's 'the' ends up in the middle, wrapped by the gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A gold belt worn about the waist makes someone look different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold round the middle' paints a belt worn at the waist; 'round' and 'middle' both describe the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as other is different or distinct, not identical.

clue.text: Quarrel about a sheer mess-up in entertainment

indicators.note: the word for a quarrel goes about the rearranged letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: a mess-up of the letters means they are jumbled

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a botched show.
explanation.walkthrough: The quarrel word is split around the jumbled letters. A raree-show was a peep show carried about by travelling showmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A raree-show was a travelling peep show, a street spectacle for amusement.

clue.text: One, Carol, the girl for making jellies

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
to carol is to sing joyfully
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl called Carol is listed as one who makes jellies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name but is the verb to sing. Isinglass is a pure gelatin from fish bladders, once used to set jellies.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a gelatin from fish, used as a setting agent in cooking and clarifying.

clue.text: Stakes in hobbies

definitions.meaning: shares held in a business
pastimes that someone enjoys

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares held in a firm are holdings in it, and pastimes are what someone is keen on.

clue.text: The Life of Mickey Mouse ?

parts.note: the process that makes a Disney cartoon character move, giving it life

explanation.surface: A title for a biography of Disney's famous mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a biography title, but the 'life' of a cartoon mouse is the craft of making drawings move; the word also means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartoons are made by giving drawings the appearance of movement, and the word also means vigour or liveliness.

clue.text: Away round the globe, imbibing ?

indicators.note: the word for away is placed round the outside of the word for the globe

parts.note: someone away is absent
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: Someone travelling around the world while drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: something absorbent soaks up liquid, which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: An absorbent material takes in liquid, as a drinker soaks it up.

clue.text: Enact, in some form, a grandsire ?

indicators.note: putting the letters into some other form means rearranging them

explanation.surface: An actor is told to perform as an old grandfather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is fodder: 'some form' rearranges ENACT plus IN. An ancient is an old man, as a grandsire is.
explanation.definitionFit: An old man was once called an ancient, and a grandsire is an elderly forefather.

clue.text: Dogs with a flipping chance

definitions.meaning: to dog someone is to follow them closely, as a detective shadows a suspect
one of the two calls when a coin is tossed

explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two senses. A coin flip is a chance outcome, heads or the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow a suspect is to follow them, and in a coin toss the reverse face is called against heads.

clue.text: The raising of glasses in short is a dubious business

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: specs is the short form of spectacles, glasses

explanation.surface: Lifting a drink in a toast is treated with suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The raising of glasses' looks like a toast, but SPECS is turned upward to SCEPS, followed by IS. Scepsis is philosophic doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Scepsis is philosophical doubt, a doubting attitude towards claims.

clue.text: Bird for raising

definitions.meaning: a tall long-necked wading bird
a machine for lifting heavy loads

explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked wader shares its name with the jib machine that lifts loads on building sites.

clue.text: This soothsayer sounds boring

indicators.note: the word sounds tells us the soothsayer's name is said like another word

parts.note: an auger is a boring tool for drilling holes

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller who is tedious to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' seems to mean dull, but it points to the drilling tool spelt AUGER; the Roman soothsayer is spelt AUGUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman augur foretold events from the flight of birds, a prophet.

clue.text: A narrowing of a slippered pantaloon's shank

definitions.text: A narrowing of a slippered pantaloon's shank

parts.words: A narrowing of a slippered pantaloon's shank
parts.note: recalls the sixth age of man in As You Like It, where the old man's hose is a world too wide for his shrunk shank

explanation.surface: An old man in slippers has legs grown thinner with age.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's 'seven ages of man' speech the 'lean and slippered pantaloon' has a 'shrunk shank'; the noun for that wasting is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking or contraction in size is a narrowing, as an old man's leg withers.

clue.text: " Far as the walk or milky way "" (Pope)

definitions.text: " Far as the walk or milky way "" (Pope)

parts.words: " Far as the walk or milky way "" (Pope)
parts.note: a gap-fill: the missing word from a line of Pope's Essay on Man, referring to the sun's path

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a blank before 'walk'. Pope's Essay on Man has 'Far as the solar walk or milky way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word describes the sun's course across the heavens, the walk of the sun.

clue.text: Lost boys found in this land

definitions.text: Lost boys found in this land

parts.words: Lost boys found in this land
parts.note: in J M Barrie's Peter Pan the Lost Boys live in a magical island land

explanation.surface: Missing boys are discovered living in a certain country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lost Boys of Peter Pan live in Never Land; the answer is the first word of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Barrie's story the Lost Boys live in Never Land, the first half of whose name is wanted.

clue.text: China's protectors of early birds

definitions.meaning: 'China's' reads as 'china is': a very thin, delicate porcelain is named after the shells of eggs
the casings that shield chicks before they hatch

explanation.walkthrough: 'China's' looks like a possessive but is 'china is'. The early birds are unhatched chicks, not early risers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine translucent porcelain is called eggshell china, and the hard casings shield unborn chicks.

clue.text: Cleopatra offered Messenger her bluest ones to kiss

definitions.text: Cleopatra offered Messenger her bluest ones to kiss

parts.words: Cleopatra offered Messenger her bluest ones to kiss
parts.note: in Antony and Cleopatra the queen holds out her hand to the messenger, telling him the bluest of these are there to kiss

explanation.surface: The Egyptian queen grants a messenger the favour of kissing her hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Cleopatra says to the messenger: 'here's my bluest veins to kiss', offering her hand, where blood vessels show blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood vessels near the skin look blue, which is what Cleopatra offers on her hand.

clue.text: Not a regular bowler, he has his fling

definitions.text: Not a regular bowler, he has his fling

parts.words: Not a regular bowler, he has his fling
parts.note: a cricket bowler who straightens the arm delivers the ball illegally, hurling it instead of bowling

explanation.surface: A man who is not a usual bowler is having a final fling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowling arm must not straighten during delivery; one who does is called for throwing, so he 'flings' the ball rather than bowls it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurler of the ball is one who flings it, and illegal bowling in cricket is called chucking.

clue.text: Musicians may get knotted

definitions.meaning: the section of an orchestra playing violins, violas, cellos and basses
lengths of cord or twine that tie in knots

explanation.walkthrough: 'may get knotted' sounds like a rude brush-off but just describes cords that tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: The violin family make up an orchestra's section of that name, and cords or twine tie into knots.
